One of the reasons we like the Savinas and Carribbeans is that they still have great flavor while bringing heat. But we've definitely found that it depends on where our plant originated as well as which generation it is as to how great or bland it tastes. We had a surprise, delicious ghost cross pop up in our bed this year, and we'll be growing more of it next year. Last year we had a ghost plant that tasted soapy and gross so we were shocked to get such a great tasting ghost this year out of the blue.

One of the tricks we've found to really upping flavor is to combine the hots with less or no heat peppers, just like you. Our favorite add-in peppers are Fresnos and Rojos. We always have at least one of those in our dehydrated, crushed peppers.

The Texas Pete style sauce we make is crazy fast and easy: 2 cups distilled white vinegar, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, 3-4 smashed garlic cloves, 1/4 onion, 60ish grams of peppers. Cook for 20 minutes, blend, then strain and you're done. Super easy, and amazing on wings. We just did a 7Pot of this and added 1 tablespoon of sugar. Tastes like a super spicy ketchup.

Our first sauce, we roasted carrots, ginger, garlic, pineapple, and onion, then cooked that with vinegar, mango, and a complete mish-mash of first of the season peppers. Some hot, some not hot. We cooked that down for around 2 hours, then strained, blended, and added salt to taste.
